item.title: What to Watch for Next in the Iran War
item.description: The United States has proved its military superiority over Iran. Whether it can secure Iran’s enriched uranium, protect the Gulf states, and encourage popular protests is a different story. The post What to Watch for Next in the Iran War appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why Iran Won’t Restore the Shah
item.description: Previous attempts to restore Middle Eastern monarchies have met with little success. The post Why Iran Won’t Restore the Shah appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Could NATO Put Nuclear Weapons in Finland? It’s Not Impossible
item.description: Finnish law has historically prohibited the importation or deployment of a nuclear weapon anywhere on its territory—but this is expected to change soon. The post Could NATO Put Nuclear Weapons in Finland? It’s Not Impossible appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: The Pentagon Went on a $90 Billion Spending Bender—with Lobster and Pianos
item.description: To avoid losing Fiscal Year 2026 funding, the Department of Defense spent $90 billion in the final month of FY2025—including millions on frivolous or luxury items. The post The Pentagon Went on a $90 Billion Spending Bender—with Lobster and Pianos appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Turkey Sends Fighter Jets to Northern Cyprus
item.description: The deployment of Turkish F-16s to disputed Northern Cyprus might have run afoul of US export restrictions that govern how its fighter jets can be used. The post Turkey Sends Fighter Jets to Northern Cyprus appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: China Is Building Fleet of Attack Submarines, Navy Intel Chief Says
item.description: China now operates 59 submarines, compared to the US Navy’s 71—but it has expressed the clear intention to catch up. The post China Is Building Fleet of Attack Submarines, Navy Intel Chief Says appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: A Russian Air Defense System Was Just Spotted in Alabama—Sort Of

item.title: How the Iran War Will Diminish Iran’s Role in Central Asia
item.description: As Iran’s energy problems grow, the Islamic Republic can no longer rely on its geography alone to attract investment from Central Asia. The post How the Iran War Will Diminish Iran’s Role in Central Asia appeared first on The National Interest.
